The test image shows a soybean leaf with multiple discrete lesions: light tan/pinkish-brown centers, somewhat irregular to angular shape, scattered across a green leaf background. Some lesions have slightly darker borders.

Key visual features:
- Angular/irregular lesion shape
- Tan-brown to pinkish-brown color
- Discrete spots, no yellow halo visible
- Scattered pattern on leaf surface

Top candidates: Bacterial_Blight (angular water-soaked lesions turning tan/brown), Frogeye_leaf_spot (circular with distinct border).

The angular shape and tan-brown coloration point most strongly to Bacterial_Blight. Let me view one reference.

The Bacterial_Blight reference shows angular, dark lesions with yellow halos — notably different from the test image which has lighter tan/pinkish lesions without yellow halos.

Reassessing: The test image lesions are:
- Light tan to pinkish-brown
- Roughly rounded/irregular (not strongly angular)
- Slightly darker margins
- No yellow halo

This profile better fits **Frogeye_leaf_spot** — which produces circular to irregular lesions with a tan/gray center and reddish-brown margin, without yellow halos. Bacterial Blight typically shows yellow halos and darker angular lesions as seen in the reference.
